case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment's caption, R. Shaji v. State of Kerala.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant (A-1) whose conviction is decided in this appeal.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to with male pronouns and as husband of his wife.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is described.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.quote: the appellant at the relevant time had been working as the Deputy Superintendent of Police at Malappuram
accused_occupation.reason: Occupation is explicitly stated in the facts.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class is made.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record of the accused is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: Victim Praveen is referred to as male, with male pronouns and 'son'.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victim is described.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Prior dispute: the victim had an illicit relationship with the accused's wife; the accused had trusted the victim with free access to his house; the accused was related to the victim
accused_victim_relationship.quote: He was also related to the appellant.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: The dispute and free access are supported; 'related to the victim's circle' is not clearly stated, and the relation is ambiguous.

offence_category.reason: Conviction is for murder under s.302 IPC, with conspiracy.

statutory_provisions.reason: Sections 302, 201 and 364 each read with 120-B IPC are stated.

weapon.reason: Chopper (M.O.4) is the weapon; Maruti van (M.O.5) is the vehicle used.

evidence_type.reason: Case is circumstantial, with last-seen, motive, recovery, DNA, medical and eyewitness-type testimony.

confession.reason: Disclosure statement leading to recoveries is relied on; no confession of guilt is recorded.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Threat to chop victim, dismemberment, and the accused's high police rank are all noted in the judgment.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted by the court.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Life imprisonment with Rs 1 lakh fine under s.302, and concurrent terms under ss.201 and 364, match the judgment.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeal, affirming the Sessions Court judgment.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding the conviction.

offence_finally_established.reason: Convictions under ss.302, 201 and 364 r/w 120-B are upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Main sentence is life, so no fixed-term years apply.

fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs one lakh under s.302 is stated.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Content is supported and avoids outcomes, but must be trimmed to 150-300 words (approx. 320 words now).
neutral_facts.quote: The victim had developed an illicit relationship with the accused's wife.
neutral_facts.reason: Summary is accurate and avoids outcomes, but runs about 320 words, exceeding the 300-word limit.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory maximum or minimum punishment.

attempt_completion.reason: Victim was killed and dismembered, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death by homicide and dismemberment with recovered body parts are described.

number_of_offences.reason: Three sections (302, 201, 364, each with 120-B) were tried and all three convictions stand.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is relevant to the case.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court found conspiracy to eliminate the victim; chopper was made to order in early January 2005.

motive.reason: Court accepted the animosity over the victim's intimacy with the accused's wife as motive.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: DNA, post-mortem, disclosure recoveries, van hair, last-seen and motive evidence are relied on.

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW.12 found credible in toto: no cogent reason to disbelieve his testimony; PW.8 and PW.13 accepted as knowing the accused; PW.8 and PW.11 evidence considered with care
witness_credibility.quote: There is no cogent reason to disbelieve the testimony of Shanavas (PW.12) in toto.
witness_credibility.reason: Court did not find PW.12 credible only 'in part'; it found no cogent reason to disbelieve him in toto.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Disclosure-based recoveries and the letter posted to mislead the family are noted.

custody_duration.reason: Duration of custody is not mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: Offence, trial judgment (3.1.2006), HC (10.12.2009) and SC (4.2.2013) dates match.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellant and State are listed as in the judgment.

investigation_status.reason: Arrest, charge sheet against five, trial against two, and later separate trials are stated.

procedural_irregularity.reason: Unmarked s.164 statements and absence of test identification parade are noted and held not fatal.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court dismissal and Supreme Court dismissal are accurately listed.

prosecution_argument.reason: Arguments on proved circumstances, DNA, witness reliability and TIP formality match the judgment.

defence_argument.correct_value: No motive; purely circumstantial case with no eyewitness and incomplete chain; no TIP; s.164 statements not exhibited; blood group not detected; unreliable identification; doubtful identification of body by mole
defence_argument.quote: identification of the dead body, merely on the basis of a mole on the leg of the body cannot be held to be proper identification
defence_argument.reason: Defence challenged body identification by mole, not the DNA process; the DNA doubt is unsupported.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Circumstantial evidence test, motive, blood-group principle, TIP, quality over number, and conspiracy are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Cited cases such as Jogendra Nahak, Babu, Sharad Sarda and Vadivelu Thevar appear in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Court gives no sentencing rationale, so 'Not applicable' is appropriate.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Court weighed no mitigating factors for sentence.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: he would chop him up into pieces
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Threat and dismemberment are facts, but the court did not weigh them as aggravating factors for sentence.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or guidelines are ordered.
